"The culture ended at around 3500 BC, when the Yamnaya culture expanded westward replacing Sredny Stog"; the Cucuteni-Trypillia page dates the Yamnaya "3300-2600 BC". [Reviewer xx-01-a, 2026-10-18: counterpart yamnaya-culture to nobody: the Yamnaya page has the culture originate "in the Don-Volga area at c. 3400 BC" and spread across the steppe "between c. 3400 and 3200 BC", so the Dnieper steppe has no heir on the map 3500..3201 BCE (Mykhailivka, Repin and the Yamnaya core have no dossier here)]

notes: Culture dossier, one page. The Yamnaya culture (c. 3500/3300-2600 BC), named as successor here and on the Cucuteni page, needs a dossier (steppe; the brief's "early Yamnaya" could not be reached within this batch's budget). The Dnieper-Donets, Mariupol and Khvalynsk cultures (5th millennium) have no dossier either, so the steppe east of the Don and the forest-steppe are nobody's land. Gazetteer: Deriivka and Serednii Stih are not places; a 140 km radius around Dnipro stands in.
